title: Linked notes without complicated setup
description: An ordinary editor with links between materials that make sense. Structure can be added to what is already written, step by step.

blocks.text: A notepad gets cramped, but a new system of tags and markup can get in the way of carrying on writing. The move to links is worth starting from material that is already familiar.

quote.text: Maybe it’s just the way our brains age, but I’m a 40yo well-educated professional in technology and education and this app is incredibly intimidating. If you don’t already work in markdown this may not be the best place to start.

blocks.text: Give an ordinary text editor and a “link to a note” action. Show the titles and short fragments alongside, so the relationship is clear without studying a graph.
One link should help you get back to the material you need. If the user doesn’t use it later, a large graph only adds the upkeep of a structure. The first test can be run on a small existing project.
